videos.title: Can France Still Afford Its Generous Welfare State?
videos.description:
France is on the edge of a financial spiral. The global surge in interest rates has exposed the country, once considered an oasis of stability in Europe’s financial markets, as one of the continent’s weakest links. France now pays more to borrow than former crisis hot spots like Greece and Italy. With government debt growing faster than the economy, the pressure on France to rein in its budget deficit has never been higher. CNBC's Liz Napolitano reports.

videos.title: What’s the risk of political violence? | Martin Wolf on the US midterms | FT
videos.description:
As Americans prepare to vote in the November 3 midterm elections, the FT’s chief economics commentator Martin Wolf asks what the result will mean for Donald Trump, the future of US democracy and America's place in the world. 

In the third of a six-part series, Martin speaks to political scientist and author Barbara F Walter, an expert on civil wars and political violence, about the risk of unrest surrounding the elections. 

Drawing on her research into countries around the world, Walter explains the warning signs of political violence, and why America's changing demographics and the struggle to hold on to political power are fuelling divisions. How close is the US to a dangerous tipping point? And can American democracy emerge from the midterms stronger rather than more divided?

To enjoy future episodes, be sure to subscribe to ‘Martin Wolf on the World’ wherever you get your podcasts. 

Host: Martin Wolf
Producer: Mischa Frankl-Duval
Senior producers: Laurence Knight and Edwin Lane
Executive producer: Manuela Saragosa
Video editor: Richard Topping
Senior Audio Engineer: Breen Turner
Broadcast engineers: Andrew Georgiades

videos.title: The 'Socialist' Bank Thriving In Trump Country
videos.description:
Progressive political candidates have clamored to launch public banks in the lead-up to the 2026 midterm elections. videos.title: Ajay Banga on AI, Jobs & Opportunity | Global AI & Digital Summit
videos.description:
At the Global AI & Digital Summit in Seoul, World Bank Group President Ajay Banga discusses the future of development, the role of digital technology, and the opportunities and challenges presented by artificial intelligence.

He discusses the importance of getting the fundamentals of digital development right, including electricity, connectivity, affordability and digital public infrastructure, and shares examples of how locally relevant AI tools are being used in agriculture, health and education.

He also explores “small AI” and the opportunity for job creation and productivity through AI, particularly for developing countries, as well as the World Bank Group’s role in helping move promising solutions from pilots to delivery at scale.

Watch the conversation to hear his vision for using technology to drive jobs, productivity, dignity, and opportunity.

videos.title: The Race To Power AI Is Reshaping America's Electric Grid
videos.description:
AI data centers are driving unprecedented demand for electricity and putting renewed pressure on America’s power grid to modernize its equipment and develop greener, more efficient sources of power. Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon are all spending millions of dollars on local infrastructure upgrades and companies like SpaceXAI are even building off-grid power plants to power their data centers.

Google says its planned 780-megawatt data center in Pine Island, Minnesota, could offer a model for powering the AI boom. In a proposed agreement with Xcel Energy, Google says it will support 1,900 megawatts of new wind, solar and battery capacity, while minimum payments and exit fees are intended to protect local ratepayers if demand falls short.

CNBC examines whether projects like Pine Island can make the grid cleaner without shifting costs to existing customers, why some energy experts argue that smaller data centers could make better use of infrastructure already in place, and how utilities’ financial incentives can complicate efforts to build less.
